newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian sugar production stifled by imports -Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Serbian sugar production stifled by imports -Tanjug.

text.p: The price of sugar in Serbia has dropped to 2.90 dinars per kilo and will soon fall below two dinars as there are now 400,000-500,000 tonnes of sugar in the country's reserves, Tanjug news agency reported Friday.

It quoted Serbian agriculture, water management and forestry minister Jovan Babovic as saying he traders' lobby which last year imported large quantities of sugar has practically stifled domestic production
Babovic said the republican government would in future protect domestic agricultural production from imports.

According to Babovic, there is a shortage of nitrogen fertilisers on the market and the government would secure semi-manufactured and raw materials for production of an additional 11,000 tonnes of fertilisers, including 8,600 tonnes of nitrogen fertilisers, in local factories.
Imports of 20,000 to 50,000 tonnes of nitrogen fertilisers have also been approved for newly grown crops and more efficient spring sowing, Babovic said.
